events.title: Delaware hit by rare November tornado
events.summary:
Meanwhile, severe thunderstorms bring hailstones the size of baseballs in Argentina

The National Weather Service in the US has confirmed that an EF1 tornado touched down south-east of Newark in the Salem Woods neighbourhood, Delaware, on Thursday. The tornado reached 160 metres wide, had a path length of 4.4 miles (7.1km) and reached estimated peak winds of up to 100mph (161km/h). There were no injuries or fatalities but windows and roofs were damaged on several homes, a large hotel sign fell on to a number of cars, and a semi truck overturned on I95. Although Delaware often experiences a few tornadoes every year, this is only the second time the state has had tornado activity in November since 1950, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. The only other November tornado recorded was in 1989.

Severe storms have also resulted in tornadoes in Argentina as well as large hailstones. A round of severe thunderstorms moved through the central Córdoba province on Friday, bringing hailstones up to the size of a baseball (about 7.5cm in diameter). Parts of the province recorded up to 73mm of rainfall in just six hours early on Saturday. Such storms are common at this time of year. Water vapour from the Amazon meeting the Andes quickly condenses, resulting in massive cloud formations often associated with heavy downpours, lightning, tornadoes and large hailstones.

Storm Charles has brought destructive weather to the Iberian peninsula this week, particularly in Portugal and the far south of Spain. Heavy rain and strong south-westerly winds arrived first in the Portuguese island of Madeira, before the system headed towards the mainland on 11 November. A wind gust of 84.5mph (136 km/h) was recorded at Funchal airport, alongside rainfall totals reaching 355mm (13.97in) in 12 hours. In Lisbon, 183 flights were cancelled on Wednesday, about a third of its normal daily traffic, while Madrid Barajas airport had 155 cancellations.

After causing widespread flooding in Spain and Portugal, the system moved on a north-easterly track through southern France and then towards northern Italy. This resulted in significant flooding in parts of Cannes, some of which caused rock falls and led to the closure of roads along the French Riviera. The Italian weather service issued a red rainfall warning, its highest level, for the area extending from Tuscany to Venezia. Further heavy rain is expected to fall in Italy and the Balkans over the next few days, with the latest forecast models indicating an additional 100mm could accumulate widely, while totals close to 200mm are likely in more mountainous areas.

Good morning. Ahead of the hotly anticipated UK-EU summit this Friday, Andy Burnham is expected to make the reset of our relationship with Europe the pivotal theme of his white-tie speech at the lord mayor’s banquet in London tonight.

The prospect of closer ties – and the possibility of going “all the way” to reversing Brexit – has been met with jubilation and relief in some quarters and vehement opposition in others, while around Westminster and across the media the psychodrama has been spiralling for weeks.

Environment | The strongest El Niño in centuries has added urgency to UN climate talks in Turkey as vulnerable countries face “compounding” crises. In other Cop31 news, queer and gay protesters defied a crackdown on LGBTQ+ rights in Turkey to lead a civil society climate march.

Thursday | German chancellor Friedrich Merz, French president Emmanuel Macron and UK prime minister Andy Burnham will be among around 20 heads of state meeting in Berlin to discuss defence funding for Ukraine, and to establish a unified position on future peace negotiations in its war with Russia.

The state-run Bahrain news agency is also carrying the statements of each country in the region responding to Iran’s actions targeting their Gulf neighbour this morning.

Jordan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar have all strongly condemned the attack and expressed solidarity with Bahrain.

The Kingdom affirms that the Iranian attacks constitute a violation of international law and the principles of good neighborliness. The Kingdom stresses the importance of an immediate halt to the blatant Iranian attacks on the countries of the region, and of taking serious steps towards achieving security and stability for the countries of the region and their peoples.

The continuation of these attacks represents a dangerous escalation that will complicate efforts to contain the tension and undermine political and diplomatic endeavors aimed at achieving security and stability in the region.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed the Kingdom of Bahrain’s strongest condemnation of the continued Iranian aggression against its territory, including the attack launched today, Sunday, November 15, 2026, by drones that were intercepted and destroyed by air defense systems in the Kingdom’s airspace.

This comes two days after a similar attack at dawn on Friday, November 13, 2026, by two drones that were also intercepted. The Iranian Revolutionary Guard explicitly claimed responsibility for these attacks. The Ministry praised the efficiency, vigilance, and capability of the Bahrain Defense Force in confronting today’s attack and its complete readiness to deter any aggression.
The Ministry considered these attacks a resumption of Iran’s heinous aggression against the Kingdom and countries in the region, disregarding the provisions of international law and the principles of the UN Charter.

While Andy Burnham may be nervous about making the debate about the future relationship with the EU a simple one about whether or not to rejoin (see 10.59am), his opponents are happy to have this argument. Brexiters have already launched a campaign called Stay Out. It is led by Oliver Lewis, who was deputy to David Frost when Frost was Boris Johnson’s chief Brexit negotiator.

Lewis was on the Today programme this morning. Making the case for the UK to stay out, he focused more on the argument that this would be a breach of promises made to the public (including by Andy Burnham during the Makerfield byelection campaign) than on the notion that Brexit has been a great success. In this, he was broadly aligned with what Kemi Badenoch has been saying.

It’s always a good idea to promote closer cooperation with all of our allies, and there’s always more that you can do to facilitate trade with friends and neighbours. However, what I disagree with is a settlement that will involve us paying hundreds of millions of pounds into the EU and involve the imposition of huge amounts of red tape on all sorts of businesses across the country … I think it’s a really bad step backwards.

events.title: Trump administration blames travel chaos on former presidents and Congress | First Thing
events.summary:
Donald Trump on Sunday blamed the Biden administration for the four-hour nationwide flight stoppage that led to thousands of canceled flights over the weekend. Plus: How Israel is using Amazon facial recognition to track Palestinians

  • Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning.

A four-hour nationwide flight stoppage on Friday threw the entire weekend into chaos, with thousands of flights getting canceled and even more delays. While air travel is expected to even out again on Monday, nearly 2,000 ​flights within, into or out of the US on Sunday were canceled and more than 8,600 were delayed.

What’s the Trump administration saying? “I take responsibility for what was given to me by prior administrations,” the US transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, told CNN’s Dana Bash on Sunday.

What has Trump said? Donald Trump did not comment on the ground stop until Sunday, when he posted on Truth Social blaming Joe Biden. “The Biden Administration was an FAA disaster. Everything they touched turned bad,” Trump wrote. “We have the knowledge and plan for the Flight Control Systems, we need Congress to give the money, FAST!”

What caused the ground stop? Duffy on Saturday said the issue stemmed from routine maintenance.

Who will he be meeting in China? China confirmed on Monday that Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin would hold their first trilateral summit on Thursday in Shenzhen.

What’s at stake here? Trump is under pressure to speak with Xi about the Nvidia fallout, in which the company’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, was forced to resign amid revelations he had had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

events.summary: Women who scored high on intelligence tests were seen as more hostile by their teammates and got less help, a new study finds. High-scoring men faced no such penalty. Research explains why.

events.title: Fears of rising antisemitism in Europe
events.summary: Holocaust survivor Regina Sluszny commemorates the victims of Auschwitz as Jewish communities across Europe face growing hostility. What does the promise of "Never Again" mean for Jewish life in Europe today?

events.title: Why the integration of immigrants in Germany remains a challenge
events.summary: The Federal Office for Migration and Refugees has released a new Integration Report. It found that while the integration of people with a migrant background is improving, violent youth remain a problem.

events.title: Democracy study: One-quarter of Germans want a right-wing authoritarian dictatorship
events.summary: The far-right AfD's electoral successes point to a new trend in Germany: Prejudice, resentment, and extremism are on the rise. A new study suggests satisfaction with democracy is at a low ebb.

events.title: Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?
events.summary: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank has a grievance redress mechanism for people affected by projects it finances. But those seeking to file a complaint face significant hurdles. Critics say reforms are needed.

events.title: Wael Mohya could make German football history at 17
events.summary: At just 17, Gladbach forward Wael Mohya has earned his first Germany call-up. The dual-national talent has chosen the DFB path for now — and could soon make modern national-team history.

events.title: Can global leaders put their money where their mouth is on climate?
events.summary: World leaders warn that geopolitical divisions are distracting from the climate crisis as negotiations focus on clean energy and financing, while Iran calls for compensation for war-related environmental damage.

events.title: DW Science explainer on the default mode network: what your brain does when you aren't focusing on anything, and why it's important.
events.summary: Doing nothing might be the ultimate brain hack. When you're bored, the brain goes into default mode network. It's not only healthy for you, but it may also shape the very essence of your identity.

events.title: Germany slips in climate protection rankings as other countries make gains
events.summary: Record renewable energy growth is driving climate progress in some countries, but Germany and many major emitters are falling behind.

events.title: British counterterrorism police arrest US soldier accused of spying on behalf of Russia
events.summary: A member of the US Army has been arrested near Gloucester in England. Police said he was suspected of espionage activity in connection with Russia. Investigators from the US and UK are involved in the probe.

events.title: UK Privy Council overrules Trinidad and Tobago gay sex law
events.summary: A London court has overturned a Trinidad and Tobago law criminalizing consensual sexual relations between male same-sex couples. As a result of the colonial legacy, it is the independent country's last court of appeal.

events.title: Victims of Nazi war in Poland call on Germany for support
events.summary: More than 80 years after the end of World War II, Polish victims of the Nazi regime are still waiting for a "humanitarian gesture" from Germany. The 2027 draft budget hasn't left them much hope for possible reparations.

events.title: Iran denies role in fridge hack, France summons ambassador
events.summary: France has said it rules "nothing" out in response to a cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration units. Iran, however, said it categorically rejected Paris' "baseless and one-sided accusations" of IRGC involvement.

events.title: Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?
events.summary: Hitler once called Eastern Europe "Germany's India." A new exhibition examines the links between colonialism and Nazism, and the bitter debate over where comparisons illuminate history and where they fall short.

events.title: Neuer injury gives Urbig chance to shape Bayern and Germany future
events.summary: Manuel Neuer's latest injury gives Jonas Urbig a run of games in Bayern's goal. Marc-André ter Stegen remains Germany’s No. 1, but Urbig now has a chance to strengthen his case for the future.

events.title: Megaspeed and the battle to go high-end Nvidia chips into China
events.summary: Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy has shone a light on Megaspeed, the company she worked for. It is under investigation in the US for smuggling Nvidia chips into China, which it denies.

events.title: Bulgaria highway pileup kills 12, dozens injured: PM
events.summary: At least 12 people were killed and dozens injured in a series of crashes caused by thick fog in Bulgaria. Police, firefighters and paramedics were dispatched to the scene for the rescue operation.

events.title: Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha and the question of religion
events.summary: Felix Nmecha's "Crowns down" celebration has drawn criticism from a Borussia Dortmund fan club, reopening debate over faith, inclusion and religious messaging in football.

events.title: Fact check: Online disinformation rife after Krakow mass shooting
events.summary: Fake and AI-manipulated images spread online in the hours after the Krakow attack, fueling false narratives about the mass shooting. DW Fact Check examined what's real, and what isn't.

events.title: Why electrification is the climate game changer we need
events.summary: From EVs and electric buses on the road, heat pumps warming homes and solar panels powering appliances, the shift to electrifying tech is already in full swing. But what exactly does "electrification" mean?

events.title: Will Australia push for fossil fuel exit at UN talks?
events.summary: The heat is on Australia as chief negotiator at the COP31 UN climate conference to forge a path away from coal and gas, and to protect Pacific neighbors facing rising sea levels.

events.title: US, Russia, Ukraine wrap up talks with prisoner exchange agreement
events.summary: Peace talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US concluded in the United Arab Emirates. The two day talks were the first such meeting since February. DW has the latest updates.

events.title: Why malnutrition can go unnoticed, and what that means for our health
events.summary: More than 2 billion people worldwide suffer from nutrient deficiencies, most of them in the Global South. The health consequences can be devastating.

events.title: Iran war oil shock drives dip in global emissions, study shows
events.summary: Global carbon emissions are expected to fall slightly in 2026, but not because of major progress on climate action. Instead, it's high energy prices following the US attack on Iran that's driving the trend.

events.title: New trilateral talks on Ukraine war in Abu Dhabi: What to expect?
events.summary: Ukrainian and Russian representatives last met in February for talks on ending the war, but the same sticking points remain. Ukraine continues to demand security guarantees, which is a non-starter for Russia.

events.title: Russia: Independent Novaya Gazeta shuts its Moscow newsroom
events.summary: The investigative newspaper is closing its doors after Russian authorities labeled it a "foreign agent" and ordered it vacate its Moscow premises.

events.title: Norway's ice hockey team says Russia replacing it at World Juniors
events.summary: The wrangling over Russia's return to international ice hockey continues, with Norway saying it has been kicked out of the next major tournament to accommodate Russia. Switzerland has joined a "boycott."

events.title: 37 years after fall of Berlin Wall: How divided are Germans?
events.summary: Three artists share their thoughts on the reunification of East and West Germany. How do they perceive a shared "we" and what gives them cause for optimism?

events.title: Germany: CDU names Ilse Aigner as candidate for president
events.summary: The steering committtee of the CDU have announced Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner as presidential candidate. This gives her a good chance of becoming the first woman to occupy the role.

events.title: Why Nvidia CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy matters for AI race
events.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has apologized for an affair with a woman the US believes was spying for China. The story could have profound implications for the world's most valuable company and the global AI race.

events.title: Who is Ilse Aigner, leading candidate for Germany's next president?
events.summary: She would be the first female president and the first Christian Social Union politician to hold Germany's highest office. Ilse Aigner is the favored candidate for the Federal Convention vote on January 30.

events.title: Germany news: Germany marks fateful date of November 9
events.summary: Germany is commemorating the Nazi-led November pogroms 88 years ago. Events are also being held to mark the anniversary of the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989. DW has more.

events.title: Germany: Chancellor Merz to nominate Aigner for president
events.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced that he will nominate Ilse Aigner for federal president, paving the way for her to be the first woman to hold the office. DW has more.

events.title: 'Never Again!': Holocaust remembrance under pressure
events.summary: Only a few Holocaust survivors remain who can share their stories firsthand. Meanwhile, voices calling for an end to what they describe as a "cult of guilt" are growing louder. How can Holocaust remembrance survive?

events.title: As COP31 Antalya kicks off, can world move beyond big promises?
events.summary: Droughts, floods and extreme heat are upping the pressure on delegates at the UN climate talks in Antalya, Turkey. Can countries move beyond pledges to concrete action?

events.title: Germany hopes to host world ice hockey championship — without Russia
events.summary: International protests continue after a court ruled that Russia must be allowed to return to international ice hockey. Germany is seeking a solution that will allow the country to host next year's world championship.

events.title: Amid protests, France's rising debt costs threaten stability
events.summary: France plans to spend an extra €4 billion on education amid nationwide protests. But with public debt mounting and interest costs climbing, how much fiscal room does the government have?

events.title: Ilse Aigner tipped by party allies as next German president
events.summary: German media reports suggest that Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner's chances of becoming the next president are on the up. Long favored by her Bavarian CSU, now it seems Christian Democrats nationwide plan to back her.

events.title: Tesla to 'wind down' production of flop Cybertruck
events.summary: Elon Musk's electric pickup for the future will start to be consigned to the past next year. The Cybertruck's bulk and crude shape meant it could only pass regulatory standards in more permissive markets.

events.title: Preparing for 45C: How Germany tests its crisis response
events.summary: A record heat wave. Five years of drought. A nation under pressure. Germany is running its biggest joint crisis exercise to date to test how authorities would cope with an escalating climate emergency.

events.title: What to know about the IIHF Women's Ice Hockey World Championship
events.summary: As ice hockey's governing body continues to wrangle over how to respond to a CAS order to reinstate Russia to international play, the top women's tournament gets underway in Denmark without Russia.

events.title: Exercise coaching boosts colon cancer survival
events.summary: Evidence suggests exercise can keep more cancer patients alive. But what does "living longer" actually mean, and who does it apply to?

events.title: European shares join a global sell-off as AI spending fears rattle Wall Street and Asian markets
events.summary: European shares have fallen after sharp losses in Asia and on Wall Street. Doubts over huge AI investments and fears of curbs following the Democrats' US midterm victory have rattled global markets.

events.title: Russia is back in world sport, but who is drug testing its athletes?
events.summary: DW has found that three-quarters of Russia's weightlifting team had no independent out-of-competition testing before this year's world championships, despite the country's doping history.

events.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement from international football
events.summary: The announcement by the footballing legend comes just weeks after a public spat with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over playing time.

events.title: What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump
events.summary: From high oil prices and data centers to tariffs and mounting debt, economic concerns played a key role in the crushing defeat of President Donald Trump's Republicans. So can the Democrats now make a difference?

events.title: Gold for the West Bank: Meet Palestinian karate champ Mariam Bsharat
events.summary: The occupied West Bank is not an obvious breeding ground for sporting success. But Mariam Bsharat, 17, has beaten the odds to become a karate world champion and is making a new life in Germany.

events.title: Harry Potter films turns 25 ahead of new TV series' release
events.summary: In 2001, "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" hit cinemas and took the world by storm. Today, anticipation for the new series is high, but its creator, J.K. Rowling, remains a controversial figure.

events.title: Leading ice hockey nations, sponsors oppose Russia's return
events.summary: Ice hockey's governing body says the impact of a court decision forcing it to reinstate Russia presents "significant practical and sporting challenges." Several leading nations say they won't play against Russian teams.

events.title: BMW reports lower Q3 earnings as China woes mount
events.summary: BMW reports a drop in profits in the July to September quarter amid fierce competition from China.

events.title: Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died
events.summary: Bear, Tiger and Tiger-Duck: The author and illustrator Janosch achieved world fame with his heartwarming children's figures. He died at the age of 95.

events.title: Could AI give NFTs a second chance?
events.summary: NFTs have plunged in value since their pandemic height in 2021. In some cases, they are worth 99% less than they were paid for. Yet tokenization of real-world assets and AI means the curios may yet have a future.

events.title: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated
events.summary: Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

events.title: How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community
events.summary: As the co-founder of the ADIRA Drag Festival, Lebanese performance artist, drag performer, DJ and cultural organizer Hassandra has become an essential part of Berlin's queer artistic landscape.

events.title: Football: Spanish player dies on after cardiac arrest on the pitch
events.summary: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel has died following a collision with the opposing goalkeeper. The Spanish second-division club has said it is "heartbroken" by the loss.

events.title: Asian Cup postponed due to Middle East conflict
events.summary: The Asian Cup has become the latest sporting event to be affected by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Organizers cite "exceptional circumstances" in Saudi Arabia, which has seen several Houthi attacks of late.

events.title: Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?
events.summary: France, Germany and Italy face a volatile bond market as war inflation bites. With US tech giants now issuing billions in AI bonds, they are competing with cash-strapped European governments.

events.title: Ice hockey officials considering options after CAS order to reinstate Russia
events.summary: Ice hockey's ruling body is deciding how to respond to a decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport that allows Russia back into international competition. Germany hasn't ruled out pulling out as a tournament host.

events.title: LA communities kick out Big Oil
events.summary: After years of advocacy from residents and legal battles with Big Oil, Los Angeles voted to ban drilling and phase out oil extraction in the city. It's the first city in the United States to kick the oil industry out.

events.title: Kimi Antonelli makes history as youngest F1 champion
events.summary: Kimi Antonelli became Formula One's youngest world champion and Italy's first since 1953 when he finished third in Sunday's thrilling and crash-hit Mexico City Grand Prix.

events.title: Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like
events.summary: What happens when your name evokes laughter or ridicule? Research points to negative life outcomes, but some people learn to embrace unfortunate names.

events.title: Germany news: Merz hopes for Korean reunification at DMZ
events.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz has expressed hope for Korean reunification during a visit to the heavily fortified border. Meanwhile, President Steinmeier has held talks with China's Xi Jinping in Beijing.

events.title: Bayern Munich's Kenya friendly highlights Africa's growing pull for global sport
events.summary: Bayern Munich are to open Nairobi's new Raila Odinga International Stadium against Ajax as Kenya prepares for AFCON 2027. The match highlights Africa's growing sports ambitions — and questions over cost and legacy.

events.title: IIHF ordered to allow Russia back into world championships
events.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ruled that Russian teams must be allowed to take part in international ice hockey tournaments. The IIHF had banned Russia following the country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

events.title: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism
events.summary: From Picasso to Andy Warhol, a surprising number of artists have portrayed the German breed. But the dachshund has also at times been co-opted as a political symbol.

events.title: Germany's Alexander Zverev clinches tennis No. 1 ranking
events.summary: Alexander Zverev is the second German man, after Boris Becker, to clinch the No. 1 spot in tennis.

events.title: 'Star Trek' star Patrick Stewart dies age 86
events.summary: The Shakespearean actor landed the role of a lifetime as "Star Trek" Captain Picard. He passed away at age 86.

events.title: India increases growth forecast for fiscal year
events.summary: India's Ministry of Finance has increased its growth forecasts for the current fiscal year. But it also warned about inflation, particularly for fuel and energy, amid continued instability in the Middle East.

events.title: Volkswagen logs Q3 operating loss of €5.86 billion on Porsche writedown
events.summary: The Volkswagen Group has filed its worst quarterly performance since the height of the "Dieselgate" scandal in 2015. Share prices climbed in response, however, perhaps because the bad news was so well signposted.

events.title: Russia shadow fleet sanctions: Can the EU act without US?
events.summary: The US is reportedly considering ways to convert "dark tankers" into legitimate vessels, allowing them to transport crude oil that is not subject to sanctions.

events.title: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany's health scare highlights the need for better support for elite coaches
events.summary: Vincent Kompany’s health concern is a reminder that elite football's pressures affect coaches too. Better support, clearer structures and mental health safeguards are increasingly vital.

events.title: Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?
events.summary: Seagrass protects coasts, shelters thousands of species and stores CO2. But some 30% of this valuable ecosystem has disappeared since the late 19th century. Can we bring it back?

events.title: EU's 'Made in Europe' push unnerves global auto suppliers
events.summary: In shielding Europe's carmakers from Chinese rivals, the EU risks hurting close partners from Turkey and Morocco to Japan and South Korea. Billions in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs are at stake.

events.title: Africa's first Youth Olympics open in Senegal amid hope and scrutiny
events.summary: Senegal is hosting Africa's first Youth Olympics, with 2,700 young athletes competing in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. The Games bring pride and hope, but also questions over cost, rights and legacy.

events.title: What Germany thinks of carmaker Audi's $4 billion deal with Trump
events.summary: The luxury carmaker is set to open its first factory in the United States — a move Trump credits to his tariffs. DW examines the German reaction amid a massive auto industry cull at home.

events.title: EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm
events.summary: The European Union wants to relax rules for pesticides, saying it will be easier for farmers to adopt more environmentally friendly options. But health and environmental experts say the risks are far too great.

events.title: Can Germany revive its economy before the far-right AfD gains ground?
events.summary: Conflicts, rising costs and Chinese competition are testing Germany's economic model like never before. Can new growth sectors create jobs and ease voters' economic fears, thereby helping contain the far-right AfD?

events.title: US sanctions target Iran's rail sector as Tehran shifts cargo from sea routes to overland corridors
events.summary: As US sanctions expand to Iran's rail sector, Tehran is relying more heavily on overland links with China and Central Asia. But capacity constraints, delays and costs limit rail's ability to replace maritime trade.

events.title: Rising emissions and temperatures: The cost of Trump's climate retreat is now clear
events.summary: The world is set to breach the critical 1.5-degree temperature limit, with Donald Trump's US withdrawal from climate action worsening the outlook, according to a UN report. But there is a small silver lining.

events.title: Brutal, revolutionary empire builder: Genghis Khan's legacy
events.summary: Berlin is host to a major exhibition on the founder of the Mongol Empire and his successors. Here's how Genghis Khan disrupted the course of history.

events.title: The homeless man living in front of a London mega-mansion
events.summary: Anders Fernstedt lives in London without any money. The Swedish native has built a most unusual home under the porch of a house worth over €200 million. How did that happen?

events.title: Excitement builds ahead of GTA VI release
events.summary: After eight years of development by Rockstar Games and multiple delays, the 6th installment of the world's most talked-about game Grand Theft Auto is being released this Thursday, November 19. The game, founded nearly three decades ago and built around stealing cars and outrunning the police, boasts some 500 million sales, and this time is preparing for yet another big score, as millions of fans around the world get ready for its launch.

events.title: Cape Verde President Neves wins second term
events.summary: Cape Verde President José Maria Neves has won a second five-year term, according to provisional results from Sunday's election, besting five challengers ​including the archipelago's ‌first female candidate after a campaign focused on the need to create more ⁠jobs for young people.

events.title: Hundreds of thousands protest Czech government's media funding plan
events.summary: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs rallied in Prague on Sunday against a government plan to cut a public media fee and move funding to the state budget — a policy critics say would dent the broadcasters' independence and viability.

events.title: Pope Leo wraps up South America tour that tested recovery from cancer surgery
events.summary: Pope Leo XIV concludes his 12-day homecoming tour of South America on Monday, a visit that has helped dispel concerns over his health following his recovery from cancer surgery. The 71-year-old pontiff visited Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, crisscrossing a continent where he had spent almost two decades serving as a missionary.

events.title: Francophonie summit avoids 'major disaster' after clash over leadership
events.summary: A summit of French-speaking nations attended by France's Emmanuel Macron postponed the election of a new chief Monday after a row between African neighbours the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda. The postponement appears to have staved off a threatened walkout by DR Congo, avoiding what would have been a "major disaster", says France 24's Philip Turle.

events.title: What is the International Organisation of la Francophonie?
events.summary: With the 20th Francophonie Summit underway in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, all eyes are on the International Organisation of la Francophonie (OIF). But what is the OIF? Resembling the Commonwealth, this post-colonial bloc unites around 90 nations, from 53 full members to friendly states drawn by political and economic ties. Liza Kaminov breaks down what the organisation is all about.

events.title: Gérard Depardieu: Cinema icon drops appeal and apologises to victims
events.summary:
French actor Gérard Depardieu on Monday withdrew his appeal against his 2025 conviction for sexual assault, acknowledging his guilt and apologising to his victims.
 
He has also been indicted in a separate case following a rape complaint, with a decision expected on November 26.

events.title: Estonia to close Russian border crossings after attempted arson attack on drone ‌maker
events.summary: Estonia will close all its border crossing points with Russia from December 1, its foreign minister said on Sunday, following a suspected sabotage attack on an Estonian drone maker that Tallinn blamed on Moscow.

events.title: Macron to inaugurate Cambodia temple after 14-year restoration
events.summary: In Cambodia, French President Emmanuel Macron and King Norodom Sihamoni are expected to inaugurate a newly restored temple at the world-famous Angkor archaeological site on Monday. After 14 years of painstaking work, the Western Mebon, a thousand-year-old monument, has been restored to its former glory. A monumental restoration effort, bringing together Cambodian and French expertise. Alix Ostian, Aruna Popuri and Constantin Simon report.

events.title: Yemen's Houthis advance on Aden as govt bolsters defences
events.summary: Yemen's Houthis were advancing on the interim seat of the internationally recognised government on Sunday, positioned just 60 kilometres from Aden, according to military sources, as government forces rushed to defend the city.

events.title: Canary Islands struggle to cope after massive influx of migrants
events.summary: Nearly 2,200 migrants have reached Spain’s Canary Islands by boat over the past two days, Spain’s maritime rescue service said on Sunday. The archipelago off northwest Africa is a major entry point for migrants, mainly from West Africa, attempting the dangerous Atlantic crossing in makeshift boats.

events.title: Ukraine strikes Crimea bridge as Zelensky says Starshield caps helping Russian attacks
events.summary: Ukraine has struck the bridge linking Russia and ⁠Crimea across the Kerch strait, limiting the flow of traffic, the peninsula's Russian-backed governor Sergei Aksyonov ⁠said on Monday. It comes after Russia struck energy and railway infrastructure across Ukraine over the weekend, in attacks President Volodymyr Zelensky said were made possible ⁠partly due to restrictions on Ukraine's use of SpaceX's Starshield service.

events.title: 'Not a minute longer': Israel's Eisenkot calls for Netanyahu's ouster
events.summary: Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot on Sunday said caretaker premier Benjamin Netanyahu "cannot remain at the head of the government for a minute longer", following press reports that Netanyahu's office tried to frame members of an Arab-Israeli party ahead of last month's election.

events.title: Francophonie summit postpones new leader vote amid DR Congo-Rwanda dispute
events.summary: The Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie (OIF) on Monday had been set to choose its new secretary general during talks in the Cambodian capital Phnom Penh. But delegates decided to postpone the election for a year after a walkout threat by the Democratic Republic of Congo amid an ongoing dispute between Kinshasa and Kigali.

events.title: Verdict week in the Myanmar genocide case
events.summary: PRESS REVIEW – Monday, November 16: The international press looks ahead to a verdict that could find the state of Myanmar guilty of genocide against the Rohingya minority. In other news, French journalists lift the lid on the many trials involving child prostitution. And finally, in Ireland, a cache of 12,000 once-banned books is back in the spotlight.

events.title: Xi, Trump and Putin to discuss 'world peace' at Shenzhen summit, China says
events.summary: The Chinese foreign ministry on Monday said that President Xi Jinping and his US and Russian counterparts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin would discuss "safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability" when they hold their first trilateral summit in Shenzhen this week. The meeting is expected to happen on Thursday on the sidelines of a summit of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders.

events.title: Nations League: France defeat Turkey to advance to quarter-finals
events.summary: France struggled at times but defeated Turkey (2-1) in the Nations League matchday. France finished first in group A1 and qualified for the quarter-finals.

events.title: 🔴 Live: 600 Ukrainian drones target Moscow, Crimea bridge strike halts traffic
Live: 600 Ukrainian drones target Moscow, Crimea bridge strike halts traffic
events.summary: Russian air defences intercepted 600 Ukrainian drones flying towards the Moscow region overnight and into Monday morning, Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin said. Ukraine also struck the bridge linking Russia and Crimea across the Kerch straight, the peninsula's Russia-backed governor said. Follow our liveblog for all the latest developments.

events.title: Five EU nations set to announce migrant deportation centre deal with Rwanda
events.summary: Five EU countries on Monday are set to announce a deal to establish a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda – the first such facility outside the bloc. The move comes after the EU toughened its migration rules in late 2025.

events.title: Eisenkot says Netanyahu ‘cannot remain’ after alleged election interference by aide
events.summary: Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot said on Sunday caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu must leave office immediately following reports of alleged electoral interference by a Netanyahu aide. The former army chief called Netanyahu and his entourage an "immediate threat to democracy", hours after representatives discussed forming a national unity government.

events.title: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs protest in Prague over public media funding plan
events.summary: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs rallied in Prague on Sunday against government plans to replace public media fees with direct state funding, which critics say threatens broadcasters’ independence. Organisers said turnout exceeded a March protest of more than 200,000, potentially making it the largest demonstration since the 1989 Velvet Revolution.

events.title: Musk, Uber co-founder join calls to reinstate Huang as Nvidia chief
events.summary: SpaceX Elon Musk and an Uber co-founder were among more than 158,000 signatories by Sunday demanding Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia chief pending an independent investigation. Huang resigned Thursday after revelations of two extramarital affairs, one with a subordinate and another with a woman accused of spying for China, ending his 33-year tenure at the helm of the artificial intelligence giant.

events.title: Mexican drug trade 'boss of bosses' Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo dies at 80
events.summary: Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, a founder of Mexico’s Guadalajara drug cartel known as the “boss of bosses”, died in hospital on Sunday aged 80 after suffering multiple organ failure, Jalisco state’s security ministry said. Imprisoned since 1989, he had been transferred from prison to the hospital two days before his death.

events.title: William and Kate land in Mumbai for Earthshot Prize trip
events.summary: The Prince and Princess of Wales have arrived ‌in Mumbai for the Earthshot Prize awards, ‌marking the couple's first official trip overseas in nearly four years.

events.title: Man jailed for life for attempted murder of children that sparked Dublin riots
events.summary: A man who attempted to murder three children - including stabbing one in the heart - as they waited outside their school in Dublin has been sentenced to life in prison.

events.title: Company caught up in Nvidia controversy launches internal investigation
events.summary: A cloud computing company facing scrutiny over claims involving tech giant Nvidia has launched an internal investigation conducted by external lawyers.

events.title: At least 17 people killed in two separate shootings in South Africa
events.summary: At least 17 people have been killed in two separate shootings in South Africa, police said on Monday.

events.title: Australian MP who lost her legs in alleged attack speaks on leaving hospital
events.summary: Helen Haines, the Australian politician who lost both legs after an alleged attack, has said she is "full of gratitude" upon leaving hospital.

events.title: Hamas says senior commander killed in Israeli airstrike
events.summary: A senior Hamas commander who helped plan and oversee the 7 October 2023 attack had been killed in an Israeli airstrike, according to the Palestinian militant group.

events.title: US asked if Ukraine would give up parts of Donbas for NATO membership, Zelenskyy says
events.summary: The US has asked for the first time whether Ukraine would withdraw from parts of the Donbas region if Kyiv were admitted to NATO, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.

events.title: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold unprecedented meeting, White House says
events.summary: The leaders of the US, China and Russia will hold an unprecedented meeting on the sidelines of a major economic summit, the White House has said.

events.title: Goalkeeper given 12-game ban for fatal collision with Tenerife striker
events.summary: Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been suspended for 12 games after an on-field collision that resulted in the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

events.title: Microsoft confirms all services are restored after global outage
events.summary: Microsoft has said that all services have been fully restored after a global outage which affected the NHS, police, schools and other services across the UK.

events.title: Cargo ship sinks off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast
events.summary: A Somali-flagged cargo ship has sunk in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea, according to the transport ministry

events.title: Gérard Depardieu drops appeal and accepts sexual assault conviction
events.summary: French actor Gérard Depardieu says he is dropping his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film set

events.title: At least 17 people were killed in separate shootings in South Africa
events.summary: Police in South Africa say at least 17 people were killed in two mass shootings on the same day

events.title: Cape Verde’s president is reelected for a second 5-year term, provisional results show
events.summary: Cape Verde’s president, José Maria Neves, has been reelected for a second term, defeating five challengers, including the country’s first female presidential candidate

events.title: Lula to govern Brazil for fourth term but faces challenges. Here’s what to know

events.summary: As opposition against data centers mounts in the United States, that's not exactly what's happening in China. The country is beefing up its data center construction across Inner Mongolia and leaning into its manufacturing edge to catch up to the U.S. on AI. NBC News' Janis Mackey Frayer reports.

events.title: Pope Leo arrives in Peru
events.summary: NBC News’ Anne Thompson reports from Peru as Pope Leo arrived in the country that became his second homeland. The Pope’s South America trip comes less than a month after he was treated for lung cancer.

events.title: Trump, Xi and Putin plan an unprecedented  meeting on the sidelines of APEC, officials say
events.summary: President Donald Trump will meet with the leaders of China and Russia on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzen, China’s tech hub, next week, an unprecedented gathering of the heads of the world’s biggest nuclear powers.

events.title: Pope Leo makes emotional return to his ‘beloved diocese of Chiclayo’
events.summary: Pope Leo XIV made a triumphant return to the Peruvian city of Chiclayo, where he served as bishop for and was affectionately nicknamed “Padre Roberto.”

events.title: Microsoft services hit by major outage across the world
events.summary: A widespread outage continued to hit Microsoft platforms including Outlook on Friday, with many users encountering trouble using their email accounts.

events.title: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills at least six people, officials say
events.summary: An Israeli airstrike on a hospital in southern Gaza overnight killed at least six people, the Health Ministry in the Palestinian enclave said Thursday.

events.title: Ukraine faces new Starshield disruptions as Trump envoys meet with Putin
events.summary: Hours after an American delegation touched down in Moscow for peace talks, Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country’s military had experienced a renewed wave of “significant disruptions” to the Starshield satellite internet service, hampering its ability to defend itself against Russia.

events.title: Megaspeed, chip firm at center of Nvidia scandal, pledges to cooperate with U.S. investigation
events.summary: HONG KONG — Megaspeed, the tech company at the center of the Chinese spy scandal that engulfed Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, said Thursday it will cooperate with the U.S. government’s investigations into the matter.

events.title: U.S. charges 3 men with plotting multiple terror attacks, including on British air base
events.summary: One of the men helped direct the planned attack against the air base while he was in a U.S. prison, according to a Justice Department indictment.

events.title: Senior U.S. Army soldier arrested in U.K. on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence
events.summary: The 41-year-old man was arrested “as part of an investigation by Counter Terrorism Policing” near the ⁠city of Gloucester, ​in the west ⁠of England, British police said.

events.title: U.S. moves military aircraft from British base amid Iran threats
events.summary: A U.S. official confirmed to NBC News that several military aircraft had left RAF Mildenhall as the security posture there had increased.

events.title: Nvidia opens investigation after CEO’s affair with alleged Chinese spy
events.summary: Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife in an employee memo. The board said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.

events.title: Russell Brand sentenced to more than 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assaults
events.summary: The 51-year-old comedian and actor was found guilty in a British court last week.

events.title: Gunman with far-right views who killed 6 in Poland shooting rampage dies in hospital
events.summary: The man, described as being his mid-20s, was shot by police during Saturday’s attack in the main square of Poland’s second-largest city.

events.title: Parents, sister of far-right Kraków shooter found dead in family home
events.summary: Three bodies found in the home of the 24-year-old shooter in Saturday’s rampage in the heart of Kraków, Poland, belonged to the gunman’s family, police said.

events.title: Gunman kills 6 in ‘terror attack’ in Poland, officials say; 3 others found dead in his home
events.summary: A gunman described as having “ultranationalistic” beliefs fatally shot six people while driving through a public square Saturday in Krakow, Poland, officials said, in what the country’s defense minister characterized as a “terror attack.” Three of his relatives were later found dead in his home.

events.title: Pope Leo, who had cancer surgery weeks ago, begins South American tour
events.summary: Less than a month after Pope Leo XIV underwent cancer surgery, he set off on what the Vatican called a “homecoming” tour of South America.

events.title: Investors try to regain their footing after tech stocks tank
events.summary: Tech stocks in the U.S. steadied Friday after suffering one of their worst routs in years, as investors weighed the prospect of an AI investment slowdown.

events.title: Wave of bomb threats against European airliners triggers diversions and tarmac searches
events.summary: No explosives have been found, and it isn’t clear who or what is behind the calls, but the threats alone have caused chaos in the skies and airports.

events.title: Clashes erupt in France as ‘Black Thursday’ protests sweep the nation
events.summary: “Everything is going up except wages and pensions,” the country’s main unions said. “Anger is immense.”

events.title: Russell Brand found guilty of rape and sexual assault
events.summary: Six women alleged that the British comedian had sexually assaulted them at his home, in hotels and public bathrooms. Brand has denied all claims.

events.title: Melania Trump calls for ‘enduring’ Russia-Ukraine peace as she hosts top officials at the White House
events.summary: Ukraine has been reeling from the worst collapse in relations with Washington since the start of the war.

events.title: U.S. Marine dies in Japan during training, military says
events.summary: The person, who has yet to be named, died Tuesday in Okinawa, the 3rd Marine Division said.
